function.name: generate_report
function.description: Generates a comprehensive report based on user activity data within a specified time frame. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_id.description: The unique identifier for the user.

start_date.description: The start date for the report period in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

end_date.description: The end date for the report period, inclusive, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

include_inactive.description: Flag to determine if inactive users should be included in the report.

report_format.description: The format in which the report will be generated.

message.content:
**Choosing the “best” ionisation method depends on what you’re trying to analyse and the constraints of your experiment.** Below is a quick guide to help you decide which technique might suit your needs. | Ionisation Method | Typical Applications | Advantages | Limitations | |-------------------|----------------------|------------|-------------| | **Electron Impact (EI)** | Small, volatile, thermally stable molecules (e.g., hydrocarbons, pesticides). | • Produces reproducible, well‑characterised fragmentation patterns.
• Widely available in GC‑MS. | • Requires high vacuum.
• Not suitable for large, labile biomolecules. | | **Chemical Ionisation (CI)** | Semi‑volatile organics, compounds that fragment poorly under EI. | • Soft ionisation → less fragmentation.
• Can produce protonated or deprotonated ions. | • Requires a reagent gas (CH₄, NH₃, etc.).
• Lower sensitivity for some analytes. | | **Atmospheric Pressure Chemical Ionisation (APCI)** | Non‑polar, moderately polar analytes (drugs, steroids, lipids). | • Works with LC‑MS.
• Handles high‑flow rates. | • Less effective for highly polar compounds. | | **Electrospray Ionisation (ESI)** | Polar, high‑molecular‑weight species (proteins, peptides, nucleic acids, metabolites). | • Very soft ionisation → preserves intact molecular ions.
• Compatible with LC‑MS. | • Requires a liquid sample.
• Suppression effects from salts or buffers. | | **Matrix‑Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionisation (MALDI)** | Proteins, polymers, large biomolecules. | • High throughput, minimal sample prep.
• Good for imaging. | • Limited to solid samples.
• Requires matrix selection. | | **Laser Ablation/Desorption (LA/LD)** | Surface analysis, solid samples. | • Direct sampling from solids.
• Minimal preparation. | • Requires laser‑sensitive instrumentation. | | **Field‑Ionisation (FII)** | Small, volatile molecules; high‑resolution MS. | • Ultra‑soft ionisation.
• Minimal fragmentation. | • Requires specialized equipment. | ### How to pick: 1. **Sample type & volatility** - *Volatile, small molecules* → EI or CI (GC‑MS). - *Non‑volatile, polar, high‑MW* → ESI (LC‑MS). - *Large biomolecules* → MALDI or ESI. 2. **Desired information** - *Structural elucidation* → EI (fragmentation) or CID in MS/MS. - *Quantitation of intact mass* → ESI or APCI (soft ionisation). 3. **Instrument availability** - Many labs have GC‑MS (EI/CI) and LC‑MS (ESI/APCI). - MALDI requires a MALDI‑TOF instrument. 4. **Sensitivity & matrix effects** - ESI can suffer from ion suppression; use appropriate chromatographic separation. - MALDI may give spot‑to‑spot variability; careful matrix choice helps. 5. **Speed & throughput** - MALDI imaging can analyse many spots quickly. - LC‑MS with ESI/APCI offers high throughput for complex mixtures. --- #### Quick recommendation | Goal | Suggested Ionisation | |------|---------------------| | **Metabolomics (small polar metabolites)** | ESI (positive/negative mode) | | **Proteomics (intact proteins)** | MALDI‑TOF or ESI (nano‑ESI) | | **Pesticide residue analysis** | EI (GC‑MS) | | **Drug screening (non‑polar drugs)** | APCI (LC‑MS) | | **Imaging of tissue sections** | MALDI imaging | If you can tell me more about the specific analyte class, sample matrix, and analytical goal, I can narrow down the best ionisation method even further!
message.reasoning: The user says: "Best ionisation method". They likely want a recommendation or explanation of ionization methods. We need to respond with helpful info. There's no tool call needed. Just answer.
